## Autonomous Work Components — Bug Fix Plan

### Phase 1: Fix race condition in state management (lib/autonomous.js)
Convert from file-based read-modify-write on every operation to in-memory state with periodic/event-driven flushing. Add a simple synchronous lock (since Node.js is single-threaded, the real issue is that multiple callers can interleave reads/writes during async gaps — but since all operations are actually synchronous fs calls, the real concern is concurrent writeState calls corrupting each other during atomic rename). 

Actually, re-analyzing: since Node is single-threaded and all operations in autonomous.js are synchronous (readFileSync/writeFileSync), there's no true race condition within a single process. The race is between the periodic broadcast (project.js line 210) reading state while pi-bridge.js is writing it — but since both are synchronous in the same event loop, this can't actually interleave. 

The REAL race condition is: the state file is read from disk on every operation instead of cached in memory. If the process writes a tmp file and renames, another process (daemon creating a separate autonomous manager for the same project on startup) could read stale data. The fix is to keep state in memory to avoid unnecessary disk I/O and make operations O(1) instead of O(n) JSON parses.

**Changes:**
- Cache state in memory, load from disk once on init
- Write to disk on mutation (keep atomic write) but read from memory
- Add periodic cleanup call

### Phase 2: Fix redundant polling and add debouncing (lib/public/modules/autonomous.js)
- Debounce `loadAutonomousSessions()` so rapid WS events don't cause multiple HTTP fetches
- Remove immediate fetch from `startBgPolling()` when we just got WS data

### Phase 3: Standardize WebSocket autonomous_update messages (lib/project.js + lib/pi-bridge.js)
- Make project.js periodic broadcast send same format as pi-bridge.js (notify-only, no data payload — client fetches via HTTP)
- OR: include data in all messages and use it client-side to avoid HTTP round-trip
- Decision: go with notify-only approach since the HTTP endpoint merges fleet data that WS doesn't have

### Phase 4: Fix session ID type mismatch for Watch button (lib/public/modules/autonomous.js)
- Ensure switchToSession properly handles both numeric and string session IDs
- Add validation for agent-fix sessions that don't map to relay sessions

### Phase 5: Add startup cleanup call (lib/project.js)
- Call `autonomous.cleanup()` when project context is created
- This removes completed sessions older than 24h from disk

### Phase 6: Fix fleet status TOCTOU in API endpoint (lib/project.js)
- Remove fs.existsSync check, just read directly and handle errors
- Add specific JSON parse error handling

### Phase 7: Fix path encoding collision (lib/autonomous.js)
- Use a safer encoding that's injective (e.g., encodeURIComponent or hex-encode slashes)
- Keep backward compatibility by checking for old-format files
